    ...$\mu$, $m_{\mathrm{glc}}$, and $m_{\mathrm{gln}}$ in the kinetic model. The cell death phase was defined after the viable cell density declined by 10% of the peak viable cell density in a cell culture run. It was assumed that $\mu = 0$ during the cell death phase. Since $m_{\mathrm{glc}}$ and $m_{\mathrm{gln}}$ are negligible during exponential growth,$^{1,2,11}$ it was assumed $m_{\mathrm{glc}} = 0$ and $m_{\mathrm{gln}} = 0$ when $d \leq 6$. In addition, the value of $m_{\mathrm{gln}}$ is a function of glutamine (Eq. 8) in mammalian cell cultures as described in literature reports.$^{11,40}$
(8) m_{gln}=\frac{a_{1}[\mathrm{GLN}]}{a_{2}+[\mathrm{GLN}]}    [code: algebraic, computes m_{gln}, code proposes constitutive]
    The DAEs were used for kinetic modeling of a batch hybridoma cell culture. $ ^{40} $ Since our cell cultures were performed in fed-batch mode with a daily bolus feed addition, the time period between two successive feedings ( $ t^{(d)} $, $ t^{(d+1)} $) was considered as a batch culture and Eq. 6 was applied to each time period as shown in Figure 1B. Although the model structure is similar to a neural network as described in the literature, $ ^{8} $ the DAEs replaced the hidden layer of an ordinary neural network. Symbols:
  m_{gln}: glutamine maintenance coefficient [10^{-12} mmol cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (computed)
  a_{1}: Constant parameter for Eq. 8 [10^-12 mmol cell^-1 h^-1] (parameter)
  [GLN]: glutamine concentration [mM] (computed)
  a_{2}: Constant parameter for Eq. 8 [mM] (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Specific growth rate is zero during the cell death phase.
  - Glucose and glutamine maintenance terms are zero when d ≤ 6.
  - Ammonia and lactate are considered in the growth-rate equation only above 90% of their thresholds.
  - The B1 mass balance is applied only after 144 h.
